title: Jade Lady Melon (Jade Lady F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Jade Lady melon is an F1 hybrid (honeydew) melon variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Jade Lady melon is an F1 hybrid (honeydew) melon variety, also sold or known as Jade Lady F1 or Jade Lady honeydew. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Known You Seed (sold in the Philippines through Harbest Agribusiness).

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Jade Lady melon is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Jade Lady F1 or Jade Lady honeydew, this is the same melon. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [melon variety finder](/crop-varieties/melon), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: 60 to 65 days after sowing (Harbest). Yield, by the seller's count: one grower reported 9 to 10 t from 0.5 ha. No trial on record checks these figures yet, so treat them as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit melon fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [damping off](/diseases/damping-off), [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [Fusarium wilt](/diseases/fusarium-wilt). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** 60 to 65 days after sowing (Harbest).
**Yield:** One grower reported 9 to 10 t from 0.5 ha.
**Fruit:** Oblong, silver green skin, light green flesh, 1 to 2 kg, brix 10 to 15.
Said to stay sweet even without wide day to night temperature swings.
Copes with very wet weather, grown all year by that grower.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: named among the honeydews most commonly planted in the Philippines, a Nueva Ecija grower had planted it for ten years, Harbest had distributed it for 18 years by 2018. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual melon on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Jade Lady melon

Muskmelon and honeydew need dry weather near harvest, or the fruit cracks and loses its sweetness. Plant so that the fruit ripens before the rains. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Jade Lady F1 the same as Jade Lady?
items.a: Yes. Jade Lady F1 is another name for Jade Lady. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Jade Lady?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
